This exact omission has been noted for `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` and some manager exports in prior findings, but a distinct missed issue remains: the boundary requires direct review of specific manager-owned immune interfaces, yet the public shim collapses all of them behind a single class export. That makes the ownership and invocation contract of immune orchestration uninspectable at the compatibility boundary. Evidence in the artifact: the module inventory explicitly says `_manager.py` contains `DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)`, but the actual import line is only `from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX: Re-export the manager-owned immune symbols that the module inventory claims belong to `_manager.py`, and make that surface explicit.

One of those two states is wrong today.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
